clue.text: Curved member made of wood, say

definitions.text: Curved member made of wood, say

parts.note: surface reading: a limb that bends outward, as a bandy-legged person has
setter's reading: a limb made from a tree's branch, a bough, which sounds like the word for a curve

explanation.surface: A bent limb carved out of timber, like a wooden leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A bough is a tree branch; a leg made of one would be a BOUGH LEG, which says the same as BOWLEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowleg is a leg that curves outward at the knee, a common bodily deformity.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a disclosure, a surprising uncovering of something
second meaning: the last book of the New Testament

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as opening the covers of a book; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a disclosure of something hidden, and Revelation is the final book of the Bible.

clue.text: Mare's nobbled — poor horse included in runners

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as something included sits within it
a nobbled racehorse has been tampered with, so these letters are tampered with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a nag is a broken-down horse

explanation.surface: A racing scandal: a mare has been doped, and a poor horse is among the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' looks like the horses in the race, but it means people who run businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Managers run organisations, so they can be called those who run things.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British national newspaper published every day
second meaning: a looking-glass in which you see your reflection

explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper; a 'daily' is a newspaper issued every day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mirror is a well-known daily paper, and a looking-glass is an old word for a reflecting mirror.

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
pent, as in pent-up, means shut in

explanation.surface: A wild young woman who has been locked away for her dissolute ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissipated money or a dissipated youth has been wasted or squandered, which is what misspent means.

parts.note: blood-coloured is red
thin films or layers of paint are coats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' looks like movies, but here it means thin layers. Redcoats were British soldiers of past centuries, named for their scarlet uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats was the nickname for British army troops of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Serpent's head creates stir — it's horned!

definitions.note: describes the snake rather than naming it

indicators.note: to stir is to mix up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of serpent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake rears its head and causes a commotion, and look, it has horns!
explanation.definitionFit: Cerastes is the genus of horned vipers of North African deserts, with a spike above each eye.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a moment, as in 'just a second'
second meaning: buying on account, informally 'on the never-never'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fast loans; the words are separate meanings. Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a very short moment of time, and also informal slang for an account or deferred payment.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the main stalk supporting a flower
second meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood

explanation.surface: Rose's chief supporter is a loyal friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective 'loyal', but here it is the verb meaning to check a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The stalk holds up the flower, and to check or halt bleeding is the verb sense of the word.

parts.note: surface reading: the rear seat of a car
setter's reading: a seat strapped onto a horse's back for the rider

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a car's rear seat; the question mark signals a seat placed on an animal's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on a leather seat fastened to the back of a horse or bicycle frame.

clue.text: Diplomatic move relates to frontier river crossing

indicators.note: something crossing another spans it from side to side, so it goes around the other piece

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a march is a border region, as in the Welsh Marches

explanation.surface: A diplomatic manoeuvre concerns a river crossing on the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches are the borderlands between England and Wales, and the river Dee itself flows along that border.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a formal diplomatic step or representation made to a foreign government.

clue.text: Fail to shear off with cutting blade

parts.note: to plough is old British student slang for failing an exam

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters go wrong into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer bungles shearing a sheep with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The ploughshare is the pointed steel part of a plough that slices into the soil.

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so these letters go crazy and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A list of birds, as if jotted in a birdwatcher's notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word looks like a bird, and all but the first are; 'Cuckoo' is the anagram signal and 'rook' supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged seabirds belonging to the petrel family, skimming low over waves.

parts.note: surface reading: he is startled; setter's reading: he is carried on an animal's back
a centaur is half horse, half man, so its name could be read as a description of a rider

explanation.surface: A man is startled when a centaur appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' is read as 'taken a back', carried on one; a centaur combines the two words of a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on a mount is a horseman, and the mythical centaur fuses the beast with a person.

clue.text: Having free time, perhaps idle about? Yup!

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are turned into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
a casual 'yes', like 'sure'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether having spare time means lounging about, and gets a cheery yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The leisured classes are those with plenty of spare hours and no need to work.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crazy person, someone a bit cracked
second meaning: read as two words, the casing around a kernel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a broken shell; 'cracked' is slang for crazy, and the second meaning splits into NUT CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls an eccentric or mad person this, and taken literally it is the hard casing of a nut.

clue.text: Perk up, dad — face life's later years!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
pan is slang for the face
old age is the late part of life

explanation.surface: Cheer up, father, and face growing old!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perk up' looks like one phrase meaning cheer up; it splits into the definition and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appanage is a perquisite or benefit attached to a rank, originally land for a royal younger son.

parts.note: surface reading: the westernmost tip of Cornwall in England
setter's reading: close to the coastline, the place where any land ends

explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is a famous headland in Cornwall, England, but here it is any coast, where land stops and sea starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore waters lie close to the coast rather than far out at sea.

parts.note: surface reading: an inset is a small extra picture or panel within a page
setter's reading: words inserted into a sentence, usually between brackets

explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself has 'maybe' set off by a comma, much like an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is an explanatory word or clause inserted into a sentence and marked off by brackets or dashes.

clue.text: Expression of surprise over habits seen in eg priories

parts.note: ho is an exclamation of surprise
uses are customs or habitual practices

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at the monks' robes in a priory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' looks like monks' clothing in this setting, but it means customs. In a down clue 'over' places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Priories are religious communities, and such a monastery or convent is called a religious house.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Soviet-designed ballistic rocket used in the Gulf War
second meaning: to move swiftly, as clouds driven by wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a group of ships, a natural partner for a missile, but it means to move swiftly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scud is a well-known short-range rocket, and to scud is to race along quickly before the wind.

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: plush means luxurious and rich
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wealthy husband has run off, an added bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an additional benefit or bonus, something added on top.

clue.text: One was revolutionary and with clear designs

indicators.note: to design is to plan and lay out afresh, so the letters are laid out in a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The French Revolution introduced its own calendar, with new month names; a calendar is also 'revolutionary' as it follows the earth's turning.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Republican calendar was a revolutionary dating system, and calendars track yearly revolutions of the earth.

indicators.note: an echo bounces sound back towards its source, so the words come back the other way

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or funny
the same slang word again, for strange

explanation.surface: A strange echo, like the burbling of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'peculiar' looks like it just clarifies which sense of 'funny' is meant, but it supplies a second copy of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A low continuous sound such as a brook's babble is a murmur.

definitions.note: the answer used as short for a designer label

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outfit needs a fashionable brand name on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rig-out' looks like one word for an outfit; it splits into fodder and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Designer goods carry a fashionable brand name, so the word describes a stylish, fashionable label.

indicators.note: going back means the joined words are read from right to left

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A political sympathiser returns with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow-traveller' looks like one term for a communist sympathiser, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit, a brand of alcoholic drink.
